source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Observer Music Monthly mai 2006 : Manchester/Liverpool 1976-77
text: Morley compare Manchester et Liverpool : les noms de groupes Manchester sont 'discrets, obliques, cherchant le sens dans les ombres' (Magazine, Fall, Joy Division, New Order). Warsaw 'never made it, possibly because they weren't that good.' La différence Warsaw→Joy Division : 'the difference between sleepwalking and exploring outer space.' Premier gig Joy Division janvier 1978, Pips Club.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Essay Kevin Cummins : Manchester comme émergence punk
text: Variante de l'essai VII pour le livre de photos Kevin Cummins. Hannett : 'local lad from the dark side of Mars, the city's Spector, the region's Eno.' Spiral Scratch : 'premier vrai disque punk britannique.' Morley présent au premier concert Sex Pistols Manchester (4 juin 1976) : ~40 personnes, pas 100. Futurs membres de Joy Division, Fall, Smiths, Buzzcocks tous présents.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Electric Circus fermeture — Warsaw marginal
text: Morley reconnaît avoir écrit 'novembre' au lieu d'octobre dans les notes de pochette Short Circuit — aveu d'imprécision mémorielle. Warsaw 'barely visible amongst all the noise, community spirit and outrage. Just about clinging on, joining in, definitely in the right place, but not yet the right time, and with the wrong name.' La mort du père de Morley (suicide 1977) se superpose à ses souvenirs de scène.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: NME live review Electric Circus 22 octobre 1977 : Warsaw 'pleasant surprise'
text: NME (22 octobre 1977) : Warsaw avait 'disparu pendant quelques mois' et 'n'avait pas vraiment manqué.' Retour : 'pleasant surprise : They've been thinking; the set was well-paced, there was some style and some force. The bass player had a moustache. I liked them and will like them even more in six months' time.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Sleeve notes Short Circuit (avril 1978) : Warsaw 'half formulated'
text: Morley dans les notes de pochette Short Circuit: Live at the Electric Circus (Virgin, avril 1978) : Joy Division listé comme 'Warsaw on the night. Representing those groups who had something to say but faltered in articulating. Half formulated.' Première évaluation imprimée contemporaine du groupe.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Changement de nom Warsaw→Joy Division : analyse Morley
text: Morley : 'Whereas the name Warsaw was flat and unexceptional, somehow bogus, the name Joy Division seemed to flow into and out of history, it seemed to have fierce, moving qualities always just hovering out of reach.' Le nom 'demanded extravagantly extreme music.' Contexte inquiétant : Rudolf Hess mentionné par Barney, cover An Ideal for Living ('Tomorrow Belongs to Me'), Barney lisait Sven Hassel.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: North by North West sleeve notes : Rafters 1978, Factory Club, Curtis en performance
text: Rafters Battle of the Bands (14 avril 1978) : Curtis furieux avec les Negatives de Morley. Groupe monte après minuit dans 'une humeur furieuse, avec intensité désespérée' → découverte par Gretton et Wilson. Factory Club 9 juin 1978 : 'In my memory, this is when and where Joy Division became the Joy Division you would recognise.' Curtis : 'There was a look in his eyes that wasn't at all like the look in his eyes when he was offstage.' Enregistrements RCA avortés (synthés day-glo rejetés par JD). 15 juillet 1978 Joy Division à Eric's Liverpool.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Morley 'pas encore convaincu' — Joy Division en devenir (1978)
text: Courte section de transition : Morley reconnaît qu'en 1978 il n'était 'pas encore entièrement convaincu' par JD. Gretton décrit comme 'endlessly amused and sardonic.' Factory Records n'existait pas encore. Saville dans une chambre 'chargé d'information sur l'histoire du design graphique.' Hannett 'working out just how to make drums sound like a burst of hail against a windowpane.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: NME live review JD Manchester 20 mai 1978 : 'dry, doomy group'
text: Première recension NME de Joy Division (3 juin 1978) : 'Joy Division were once Warsaw, a punk group with literary pretensions.' An Ideal for Living : 'structurally good, though soundwise poor.' 'They're a dry, doomy group who depend promisingly on the possibilities of repetition, sudden stripping away, with deceptive dynamics.' 'They have an ambiguous appeal, and with patience they could develop strongly and make some testing, worthwhile metallic music.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: NME live review JD Manchester 4 septembre 1978 : 'learnt to sculpt'
text: NME (9 septembre 1978) : 'In months, they have matured considerably. They have learnt to sculpt, not merely to emit. From a punk group with minimal awareness, to a music group with eloquence and direction.' Curtis : 'reacting to the music as if on a hot plate...Not tuneless, not tuneful. Flat and intent, a fourth instrument.' Paroles perdues dans le live — 'they may be advocating a police state for all the listener can discern.' 'This could be Joy Division's peak. On the verge of a compromise — or on the verge of something greater?'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Factory Records fondation, Erasmus, Factory Sampler preview NME (2 déc. 1978)
text: Factory comme 'extravagant sitcom' : Wilson (mythmaker), Saville (visionnaire), Hannett (technicien traumatisé), Gretton (pragmatiste stoïque), Erasmus (mystère pur). Preview NME 2 décembre 1978 : Joy Division produit par 'Martin Zero' (Hannett). Wilson a utilisé l'héritage de sa grand-mère pour payer le pressage du Factory Sampler. Profit : 'environ £80.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: NME record review A Factory Sampler 31 mars 1979 : 'Digital' et 'Glass'
text: NME (31 mars 1979) : 'Two patient, intent pieces, "Digital" and "Glass"...Two blurred depictions of desperation and desolation, the missing link between Elvis Presley and the Banshees.' Joy Division 'individual group' demandant un label 'aware.' Factory Records : 'joke as much as they poke. They are not pretentious, they are affectionate.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Première interview NME Joy Division (janvier 1979) et première couverture Ian Curtis
text: Interview au Brunswick pub : 'pauses, soupirs et sentiment qu'ils ne pouvaient pas attendre que ça finisse.' Curtis traînait sur une cigarette. Gretton regardait avec 'twinkle in his eye that wasn't necessarily completely benevolent.' Curtis : 'instinctively ensuring a kind of secrecy.' Photos dans la neige Manchester (Cummins) → première couverture NME début 1979. 'The pure, indelible stare of Ian Curtis slipped onto the cover.' Curtis 'looked like the star.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Réception d'Unknown Pleasures : 'le plus grand album jamais fait'
text: Morley : 'I think it is the greatest album ever made.' Hannett : 'the Eno, the George Martin, the Phil Spector of the piece' — 'space as a fifth instrument' — 'the sobbing, stabbing bliss of precision.' UP troisième au sondage NME 1979. Titre UP = 'Inside/Outside' dans les notes de Curtis. Titre 'Nothing' (livre Morley 2000) vient de 'I Remember Nothing'. Troisième album hypothétique : 'electronic, far darker. He was slipping from Kraftwerk to Throbbing Gristle.' Bernard Sumner : idée de la pochette UP.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Morley entend LWTUA live pour la première fois (Univ. of London, 1980)
text: Morley entend LWTUA pour la première fois : 'I knew instantly more and more people were going to hear the song, so thrilling in its desolate simplicity, its sense of solitude and atomic aloneness.' Curtis sur scène : 'in grey flannel trousers belted high on his waist, hair freshly washed, strapped on his white teardrop guitar.' Conversation banale avant le show — le sujet suicide/père de Morley jamais abordé.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: NME live review Univ. London 8 février 1980 : Curtis 'trapped butterfly'
text: NME (16 février 1980) : Curtis : 'comical trapped butterfly flapping the only real stage movement, a visual representation of the struggle.' LWTUA : 'one hell of a classic — bass, synth, drums, voice, Curtis hugging a white guitar but rarely using it. A staggeringly melodic and momentous piece.' Isolation : 'more withdrawn and estranged; reveals Numan and Foxx as true fools.' Encore : 'dislocated and depraved improvement upon Bowie's "Heroes".' Nouvelles chansons : Colony, Sound of Music identifiés.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Interview survivants 1991 : épilepsie de Curtis dans la voiture
text: Dialogue verbatim (documentaire New Order 1991) : Bernard raconte la crise d'épilepsie de Curtis dans la voiture en tournée → Luton Hospital. Stephen Morris : 'I knew he'd be alright' (sheepish) après avoir été plus upset par ses cigarettes que par l'état de Curtis. Peter Hook : 'You bastard, Steve.' Mécanisme de défense psychologique : ton comique, 11 ans après.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Closer : enregistrement Britannia Row, témoignages des survivants (2006)
text: Morley en Inde avec Police pendant l'enregistrement de Closer. Britannia Row Studios, 18-30 mars 1980, 12 jours. Hook : 'songs came quite quickly — a song a fortnight. We imagined them.' Morris : 'took longer than UP but only about twelve days.' Gretton : politique 'no wives and girlfriends.' Sumner/Hook/Morris dans un flat, Gretton/Curtis/Hannett dans un autre. Morley analyse les survivants : Bernard 'impatient'; Morris 'stunned chuckle'; Hook 'plus blessé, le plus fier.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Morley rédige l'obituaire de Curtis — parallèle avec le suicide de son père
text: Morley : 'I found the piece extremely difficult to write. I did not admit to myself that this was because by writing about such an event, I was not only writing about my favourite rock band and the awful death of their singer, but about the suicide of my father.' L'expérience du suicide personnel créait 'presque l'opposé de la connaissance.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: 'Don't Walk Away in Silence' — obituaire NME 14 juin 1980
text: Obituaire NME 'Don't Walk Away in Silence' (14 juin 1980), co-écrit par Morley et Adrian Thrills. Ouverture : 'So why do we get so animated and enthralled by Joy Division? Rock is such an infuriating thing.' Document primaire de la première réception post-mort. Co-écrit 'because I knew that I had to finish it' — ce qu'il essayait de dire 'was something to do with love.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Tony Wilson montre à Morley le corps de Curtis (Macclesfield)
text: Wilson confirme (section LXI) : 'I knowingly shoved Paul and his girlfriend in the car and drove them up there. Unlike in 24 Hour Party People, I didn't take Paul in to see the body. I wasn't so crass, I had some respect — but I wanted him to be part of it. I knew one day he would have to write the story.' Geste calculé → commissionnement à long terme de Piece by Piece. Scène différemment représentée dans 24HPP (Simon Pegg).

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Extrait de Nothing (Faber, 2000) — le cadavre en cercueil
text: Extrait de Nothing (Faber, 2000) : Morley décrit avoir vu un seul cadavre dans sa vie, dans un cercueil ouvert. 'I have only seen one dead body in my life and it wasn't the body of my father.' — implication : c'est le corps de Curtis. Prose mémorielle de qualité littéraire.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Rob Gretton — 'We've all got our idiosyncrasies'
text: Rob Gretton (interview 1991, documentaire New Order). Neil Tennant : Gretton 'never smoothes things over but makes things difficult — so that the group never forget how they began, fighting for their right.' Hook : Gretton retenait volontairement l'argent pour 'keep them hungry, keep them angry.' Rob : 'We've all got our idiosyncrasies.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Morley reprend l'écriture après Curtis — articles NME sur la scène Factory post-Curtis
text: Morley cesse d'écrire sur Joy Division après la mort de Curtis. Continue à couvrir A Certain Ratio (NME sept. 1980), OMD, Cabaret Voltaire — 'business as usual' tandis que Joy Division 'shattered into a million pieces.' L'expérience de voir le corps de Curtis est 'mise de côté' mentalement. La continuité de l'écriture était une forme de déni du deuil. Textes NME contemporains documentant la scène Factory/Manchester post-Curtis.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Morley chez ZTT (1983-1985) — Factory comme modèle, Joy Division maintenu à distance
text: Trevor Horn appelle Morley : 'Would you like to invent a record label?' Morley rejoint ZTT fin 1982. Son apport directement inspiré par Factory Records : 'concepts, publicity, marketing, theories, energy, designs, various amounts of ranting and raving, cataloguing, myth making.' ZTT comme 'excessive and absurd testimonial to the unruly ideals of Factory.' Horn comme Eno/George Martin/Phil Spector de ZTT. 1984 : Frankie Goes to Hollywood, plus grosses ventes des années 1980. ZTT a rapidement perdu son idéal post-Factory pour devenir 'more tabloid enterprise.' Pendant cette période, Morley n'écrit 'sur Joy Division que si on me le demandait.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Pre-Face (An Ideal for Living, 1984) — Morley et Warsaw : le rendez-vous manqué
text: Morley dans 'Pre-Face' (1984) : il était censé être producteur de la première session d'enregistrement de Warsaw, mais n'est pas venu (ressac d'une soirée). 'In my memory, and it might well have happened' — aveu d'incertitude précoce. 'I was the writer. They were the group. It was not written in the stars that I produce them.' Joy Division décrits comme 'drunk on luck before anything else.' Morley se qualifie de 'minor character in a minor Beatles biography.' Sa contribution : 'I mentioned Joy Division often enough for everyone nearby to know of them.' Sur l'écoute de JD : 'I am inclined to believe that one should only listen to Joy Division when one is in a euphoric state of physical and mental health.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Notes pochette Palatine — Transmission 'greatest song ever written', Atmosphere interdit NME
text: Trois notes de pochette Factory Palatine. Transmission (XLV) : Morley attaqué par skinheads après concert Secret Affair, rentra avec entaille de Stanley knife, joua Transmission '50 fois de suite.' Conclusion : 'The greatest song ever written.' Love Will Tear Us Apart (XLVI) : disc-jockey Ray Teret passait LWTUA en discothèque — pont entre JD underground et grand public. Atmosphere (XLVII) : 'The NME banned me from ever writing about this song.' — 'they said I would send people to sleep, or worse, to another paper. I told them to fuck off.' Conclusion après l'hyperbole : 'it's nice, isn't it?' — ironie assumée.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: 1997 — Jon Savage demande notes compilation JD — déclin de la critique musicale des années 1990
text: 1997 : Jon Savage demande à Morley des notes pour une compilation Joy Division, 'to be packaged by Peter Saville as a deluxe reference book.' Réflexion de Morley sur le déclin de la critique musicale dans les années 1990 : articles plus courts, stars et ticks, 'no room whatsoever for investigations of inner worlds.' 'Suggestions that the bass guitar sounded as though it were surrounded in death's foam would cause magazine editors to assume you had lost your mind back in the punk rock wars.' Joy Division 'ghosted through all these changes, unperturbed by new genres, new styles, new innovations, a law unto themselves.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Listen to the Silence (1997) — Joy Division comme Elvis de Morley pour les ténèbres, influences exhaustives
text: Morley dans 'Listen to the Silence' (1997) : 'Joy Division are like my Elvis Presley.' Bolan = face lumineuse de la vie ; Joy Division = face sombre et future. Catalogue d'influences : Kraftwerk ('gaunt tick-tock motion'), Iggy/Stooges ('hyperactive and gormless artistry'), Can ('jelled indulgence'), MC5, Velvet Underground, Bowie/Eno sur Low et Heroes, Pink Floyd. Curtis : 'His lonely, tormented images and restless stories were generated by acute self-consciousness and they low-lit the songs with their own dead level uniqueness, and polluted them with barely suppressed, terribly sourceless and ultimately exhilarating dread.' Factory Records : 'not so much a record company, more an existential bodyguard — a combination of villain, pantomime dame, benefactor, wicked stepmother, clown, love, butler, coach, pervert and performance artist.' Gretton : 'loved the group like a child, like a brother, like a father, like a friend, like a fan.'
concepts: Factory comme garde du corps existentiel

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Because — liste analytique-poétique des raisons de la signification de Joy Division
text: Morley construit une liste de clauses 'because' : 'because of the sudden visions about the value of life that Curtis had during epileptic fits' — confirmation de la valeur cognitive attribuée aux crises. 'because Hannett emptied the space of a song in order to let the listener inhabit it.' 'because Hannett combined intense inwardness with a proliferation of sensual data.' Wilson : 'decided that since we shall never know why we are alive he must select an arbitrary purpose and stick to it.' La section se termine par l'annonce que 'the story became a film' — anticipant 24 Hour Party People. Personnage 'broadly based on me' joué par Simon Pegg.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Reportage tournage 24 Hour Party People (Guardian, 2001) — Curtis ghost, Coogan/Wilson, Sean Harris comme Curtis
text: Morley au tournage de 24HPP à Manchester : voit deux fois un homme qui lui ressemble à Ian Curtis marchant dans les rues. Coogan comme Wilson : 'He does a bit of Wilson for me, and he's as camp and as breathless as the real thing.' Wilson lui-même : 'It's all untrue, which is good! I always quote Howard Hawks — between legend and truth always choose the legend.' Sean Harris comme Curtis : 'apparently unbelievable at doing the possessed Curtis dance, where the quietest of men would suddenly explode into compressed derangement. Shyness transported into a kind of flight.' Simon Pegg joue 'vague, nervy writer' reluctantly dragged by Wilson to see the dead body of Curtis.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Essai Peter Saville (Frieze, 2003) — Unknown Pleasures comme 'visual sound, processed memory, static movement'
text: Morley sur la pochette d'Unknown Pleasures : 'With such a sleeve there was no way that the music could not be important.' Pochette décrite comme 'visual sound, processed memory, static movement, collapsed space, smooth friction, tuned time, detailed nothing.' Premiers posters Saville sur les murs de Morley : 'two posters, a black and white poster advertising a gig at the Factory Club, and a yellow and white poster. They were in fact just a list of names and words, an arrangement of type, text and space, and yet they seemed to me to be art.' Saville : ayant changé 'the look of things so that he could find somewhere to hide.' Style de l'essai inspiré par Ballard : numérotation des paragraphes.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: City Life 2003 — Curtis comme plus grand chanteur de Manchester, danse et sérieux total
text: Morley répond à City Life Manchester 2003 : Ian Curtis est le plus grand chanteur de Manchester — litanie conditionnelle répétée. Curtis : 'his life was serious, the love in his life was very serious, his death was serious.' Curtis 'sang deeper harder louder wilder sweeter quicker' que Devoto, Shelley, Smith, Morrissey, Brown, Gallagher. Sa danse : 'dancing in your own world, dancing for an audience to know just how much you're in control of being out of control.' Comparaison avec Hendrix, Cobain, Morrison, Lennon : 'his name fits, and it fits for a reason, the reason being, he was serious about belonging on that list even when he was just a singer in a local Manchester rock band called Warsaw.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Wilson meurt pendant l'écriture — Wilson sur sa relation avec Morley et le commissionnement du livre
text: Wilson dans l'article Independent (31 août 2003) : 'I'm aware that it's self-consciously Machiavellian. I almost feel guilty about thinking, at that moment [du wake de Curtis], "Paul is the writer of our generation. One day he'll have to write the story."' Wilson confirme qu'il a emmené Morley à Macclesfield mais n'a pas montré le corps : 'I wasn't so crass, I had some respect — but I wanted him to be part of it.' Wilson-Morley : 'we're not friends, but you're aware that you're comrades-in-arms.' Wilson sur Curtis : 'I loved him, but I was kind of a business partner, and a comrade-in-arms, and slightly in awe.' Wilson meurt pendant l'écriture de Piece by Piece.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Observer Music Monthly sept. 2007 — Control (Corbijn), Sam Riley morphé en Curtis, Morris deux fois filmé
text: Stephen Morris : n'a 'jamais vraiment récupéré' du suicide de Curtis — et maintenant 24HPP et Control ont transformé sa vie en film deux fois. Sam Riley a décroché le rôle de Curtis à 26 ans, le jour de son anniversaire. Corbijn venu en Angleterre en 1979 'en partie à cause de Joy Division.' Riley : 'I half-morphed into what was going on within the film, and there was a kind of crash.' Riley a ensuite déménagé à Berlin avec Alexandra Maria Lara (actrice jouant Annik Honoré dans le film). Hook : 'Can you believe that the film Ian went off with the film Annik?' Hook sur LWTUA dans une discothèque à Singapour : 'people were going absolutely crazy. What's that about?'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Fragments 1987-2007 — dernière vue de Curtis par Hook (joyeuse), Sumner et pochette UP, Gretton et le silence
text: Collection de fragments analytiques : 'The last time Peter saw Ian they were together in the front of Peter's car and they were leaving for America in a couple of days and they were happy and excited, they couldn't believe their luck, and Ian was dropped off at his mum and dad's house.' — dernière rencontre Hook-Curtis : joie. 'Of course, in the end, it was Bernard, a former graphic design student, who came up with the idea for the cover of Unknown Pleasures.' — Bernard Sumner comme auteur de l'idée de la pochette UP. 'Gretton grinned, and grinned, and eventually pulled them out of interviews, deciding their silence would seem more mysterious, and winning, than their stilted pause-packed conversation.' 'When we talk about the past we lie with every breath we take.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Formation New Order après la mort de Curtis — Gillian Gilbert, nom Khmer Rouge, Bernard comme chanteur
text: Gretton aux funérailles : 'At least this means that in an awful sort of way Joy Division's future is ensured. People will still be remembering you in ten years time.' Décision de continuer : 'taken within days — within minutes, perhaps.' Morris : 'I think it actually says a lot about the strength of Joy Division that even when one of us killed themselves, we just decided we would still be a group.' Gillian Gilbert : déjà dans la communauté, avait joué avec JD un soir à Eric's Liverpool. Morris : 'If we got another singer in, it would just look like Joy Division Two... So we had to have the singer sweepstakes and Bernard drew the short straw.' Bernard : 'I didn't see it as being difficult taking over from Ian. I saw it as an honour really.' Nom New Order : Gretton l'a trouvé dans un article sur les Khmers Rouges.

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Introduction documentaire Neworderstory (1991) — Joy Division vers New Order, Factory et anti-stardom
text: Introduction rédigée par Morley pour documentaire New Order (1991), lue par Jenny Seagrove. Joy Division : 'their distressed songs about depravity and deprivation seemed to shake and writhe out of deep, craven trouble. Their music was ... fantastic.' Sur le suicide de Curtis : 'their singer Ian Curtis, snagged on the jagged edge between the pleasure of it all and the pain, killed himself. This was some end.' New Order : 'wanted resounding glamour and chaste anonymity all at once.' Factory : 'the only record label on earth romantic enough to let the group do as they pleased, how they pleased, when they pleased.'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: NME live review New Order Heaven 9 fév. 1981 — Morley pleure à l'entrée, JD songs au soundcheck
text: Recension NME (14 fév. 1981) : Morley 'burst into tears when New Order appeared onstage.' '10,000 people went after tickets; 1,000 got in.' Premières dates : New York avant Londres. Gillian Gilbert 'grafted into the group' — guitare et claviers. Au soundcheck uniquement : snatches instrumentaux de 'Transmission', 'Control', 'Atmosphere', 'Dead Souls'. Voix de Bernard : 'boyish, fragile, uncomfortably mannered.' Morley sur le set : 'the music lilted and lifted, reminding me of those tough and regular instrumental patterns in songs like Dead Souls, of the dramatic richness and indefinable structural grace of works like Atmosphere.' Conclusion optimiste : 'New Order will be great!'

source_label: S37 — Morley, Joy Division: Piece by Piece, 2008
title: Clôture du livre — Joy Division comme aide à la mémoire, dédicace Triple (Tony / Ian / Martin)
text: Clôture de Piece by Piece : 'I knew that ultimately I would think of an ending because eventually I would think of a beginning. / I knew that ultimately I would think of a beginning because eventually I would think of an end. / Joy Division would help me work it all out. / They would help me remember what happened.' Dédicace finale (Acknowledgements) : 'For Tony / And for / Ian / And for / Martin' — Wilson (mort pendant l'écriture), Curtis, Hannett (mort en 1991). Triple monument involontaire.
